claims.claim: Port-preserving node sign switching, with corresponding record, birth and noise transformations, conjugates the native reader.
limitations: Per-read marginal equivalence under centered sign-invariant noise; untransformed shared RNG coupling is not pathwise equivalence.

claims.claim: Exact surviving-overlap alignment exists iff all ratio cycles are positive and all pinned-node path constraints agree.
Free alignment bits are identifiable for task marginals up to whole-hybrid port-preserving switching; remaining ambiguity dimension is rank([M,T])-rank(M).
All 128 fixed donor pairs fail exact cycle consistency before pin constraints.
Every retained contradictory cycle touches a fallback edge; all joint-contrast overlaps are cycle-consistent, but only 32 retain port-preserving feasibility.
A conventional approximate repair rule might make donor grafts useful despite exact obstructions.
